plugins._comment: @capacitor/keyboard is installed and its events drive the layout. An earlier comment here claimed keyboard handling was done by the SparkleInsets native plugin padding the WebView by the IME inset — that padding was removed from SparkleInsetsPlugin.java, so it described a mechanism that no longer existed, and the plugin was not installed either. resize is 'none' rather than 'body' because this app sizes its shell in dvh in 45 places (AppScreen.tsx, PullToRefreshProvider.tsx, and the modals), and dvh is viewport-relative: shrinking <body> would not reach any of them, so resize:body would look configured while doing nothing. The keyboard height is instead taken from keyboardWillShow/keyboardWillHide and applied to --ime-height, which is the device-independent signal; see frontend/src/services/keyboardHeight.ts. The SparkleInsets plugin is retained only for the status and navigation bar insets. resizeOnFullScreen MUST stay false: KeyboardPlugin.java reads only that flag on Android (setResizeMode/getResizeMode are unimplemented, and the resize mode is never consulted), so with it true the plugin sets frameLayoutParams.height on the WebView's container in onStart — it resizes the WebView itself on every keyboard show, on top of --ime-height shrinking KeyboardSafeContainer. That is the double adjustment MainActivity warns about, and it squeezes the chat layout twice. resize:'none' looks like it prevents this but does nothing on Android; only the false flag does.
